title.narrative: Restoring Shelter Safety and Dignity: Integrated Emergency Shelter, NFI, and Technical Support for Displaced and Returning Households in Gaza City and Khan Younis

description.narrative: ltpgtThe ongoing humanitarian crisis in Gaza continues to leave thousands of displaced and returnee households living in damaged homes, overcrowded shelters, and inadequate living conditions with limited access to essential household items and basic shelter improvements. Many families have lost household assets, furniture, cooking facilities, and basic shelter components, affecting their safety, dignity, hygiene, and overall well-being. Women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and chronically ill individuals remain disproportionately affected.ltbrgtTo address these needs, the Palestinian Housing Council (PHC) proposes the project “Restoring Safety and Dignity: Household Shelter Support and Technical Assistance for Displaced and Returnee Households in Gaza City and Khan Younis.” The project combines household-level assistance with targeted shelter improvement support through two complementary components.ltbrgtThe first component will improve living conditions for vulnerable households through the distribution of 100 locally manufactured Kitchen Shelter Units, 100 Kitchen Kits, and essential household shelter furniture for 500 households. The intervention aims to improve food preparation conditions, household organization, hygiene, safety, accessibility, and dignity through locally produced and procured solutions. Household packages will be tailored based on vulnerability and needs assessments to ensure that assistance responds to the specific priorities of affected families.ltbrgtThe second component will support 700 returnee households living in partially damaged homes through technical assessments, household-level technical assistance, locally procured framing kits, and community-based shelter improvement works implemented through a Cash-for-Work modality engaging 70 skilled and semi-skilled workers. The intervention will support installation of doors, windows, internal partitions, and other minor shelter improvements that enhance privacy, protection, accessibility, and safe use of living spaces. Assistance will be guided by technical assessments conducted by PHC engineers to ensure that support is needs-based and appropriate for each household.ltbrgtThe project places strong emphasis on protection mainstreaming, accountability to affected populations, gender inclusion, and disability inclusion. Vulnerable groups will be prioritized through transparent selection criteria, while feedback and complaint mechanisms will remain accessible throughout implementation. The intervention also promotes localization by utilizing local workshops, suppliers, labor, and locally available materials, contributing to local economic recovery while reducing dependency on external supply chains.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented over 12 months in Gaza City and Khan Younis and will be supported by PHC’s established technical, logistics, MEAL, and community engagement capacities. Through integrated shelter assistance, technical support, accountability mechanisms, and community participation, the project will contribute to restoring dignity, improving living conditions, and strengthening the resilience of vulnerable displaced and returnee households.ltbrgtlt/pgt
